habit.lifeForm.basis: RHS plant record: "A deciduous climber of herbaceous habit with profuse flowers once established."

habit.climbsBy.basis: RHS plant record, of the genus: "mostly climbing by twining leaf-stalks".

habit.heightM.basis: Clematis on the Web: height 2.0-2.5 metres. Graham Rice for the RHS gives the same; the RHS record's ultimate-height band is 2.5-4 m; the International Clematis Society gives 2.5 m, and 3 m in warmer climates.

stem.youngDiameterMm.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Taken from its parent Clematis texensis: stems "on new growth to 3.5 mm diameter" (A. C. Gibson, Vascular Plants of Williamson County, https://w3.biosci.utexas.edu/prc/K12/pdf/Clematis%20texensis).

stem.surface.value: six-sided and finely ridged, tough and wiry
stem.surface.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Gibson, of the parent C. texensis: stems "somewhat 6-sided and inconspicuously 12-ridged ... tough".

value: purple-red on the side towards the sun
stem.colourYoung.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Gibson, of the parent C. texensis: "green often tinged purple-red on upper side". Photographs of the cultivar (Wikimedia Commons, Category:Clematis 'Princess Diana') show maroon-purple stems, leaf stalks and flower stalks.

stem.internodeLengthM.basis: Not published for the cultivar. In the parent C. texensis the internodes are "to 190 mm long" (Gibson); the cultivar's are taken as 8 to 16 cm. The same range as organs.leafSpacingM in the growth model.

leaf.arrangement.basis: A character of the genus, plain in every photograph of the cultivar but stated in no description of it that was read. Gibson, of the parent C. texensis: "Leaves: opposite decussate".

leaf.division.basis: RHS, of the Texensis Group: "deciduous climbing shrubs or subshrubs, with usually pinnate leaves".

leaf.leafletCount.basis: Leaves of three leaflets and of five are drawn. Three is published for the cultivar ("pinnately trifoliate": University of Nebraska-Lincoln Gardens, as Wikipedia cites it, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clematis_%27Princess_Diana%27); five is from photographs, between that and its parent C. texensis, which has four to eight leaflets (Bean, https://www.treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/clematis/clematis-texensis/). No flora gives a range for the cultivar.

leaf.leafletShape.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Bean, of the parent C. texensis: leaflets "ovate to roundish ... usually heart-shaped at the base". Photographs of the cultivar show broadly ovate, pointed leaflets with a rounded to heart-shaped base.

leaf.leafletLobing.value: mostly unlobed, sometimes with one or two lobes at the base
leaf.leafletLobing.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Bean, of the parent C. texensis: "sometimes two- or three-lobed"; Gibson: "mitten-shaped with 1-2 basal lobes". A mitten-shaped leaflet shows in a photograph of the cultivar.

leaf.leafletMargin.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Bean, of the parent C. texensis: "not toothed". Photographs of the cultivar show no teeth.

leaf.leafletLengthM.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Bean gives "1 to 3 in. long" for the leaflets of the parent C. texensis; against its 5 to 6 cm flowers in photographs the cultivar's leaflets are in the upper part of that, 4 to 7.5 cm.

leaf.leafletWidthToLength.basis: Judged from photographs of the cultivar: a leaflet about 6 cm long is about 4.5 cm wide. Gibson's leaflets of the parent species are as wide as long or wider (25-55 x 35-65 mm).

leaf.stalkLengthM.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Gibson, of the parent C. texensis: "petiole channeled, to 55 mm long".

leaf.leafletStalkLengthM.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Gibson, of the parent C. texensis: petiolule "to 40 mm long"; Bean: each leaflet stalk as long as its blade or longer. Photographs of the cultivar show shorter stalks to the side leaflets.

leaf.colour.basis: International Clematis Society, Clematis of the Month, August 2005: the leaves are light green and set off the flowers. Photographs show a mid green with a faint grey cast, paler beneath. Its parent C. texensis is glaucous (Bean); the cultivar is less so.

leaf.surface.value: smooth, with a net of veins and three main veins from the base
leaf.surface.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Bean, of the parent C. texensis: "well-marked, net-like veins, nearly hairless"; Gibson: "pinnately veined with 3 veined at base". The net of veins shows in photographs of the cultivar.

inflorescence.position.value: on the current year's growth, on long stalks from the leaf joints and the shoot tip
inflorescence.position.basis: RHS, of the Texensis Group: "flowers on the current year's growth in summer and autumn". That the stalks come from the leaf joints, two to a joint, is Gibson's account of the parent C. texensis ("cyme, terminal on axillary shoot, 1-several-flowered ... 2 cymes per node").

inflorescence.held.basis: Clematis on the Web: "Bright pink outward facing trumpet-shaped flowers". RHS, of the Texensis Group: "erect or nodding". The growth model's names section records the same thing as flowerHeld: upright.

flower.sizeMeasure.value: length of one flower, from its base to the tips of its tepals, its stalk not counted
flower.sizeMeasure.basis: What organs.racemeLengthM in the growth model measures for this taxon, and so what RenderFlower.lengthM carries and the flower model is authored to: one unit of the model is this length.

flower.lengthM.basis: RHS plant record: "flowers to 6cm in length". Clematis on the Web: tepals 5 cm long.

flower.diameterM.basis: Clematis on the Web: flower diameter 5-7 cm, which is the flared flower seen from the front. The International Clematis Society gives 6 cm; the Chicago Botanic Garden trial 3 inches.

flower.shape.value: tulip-shaped, flaring to a trumpet as it ages
flower.shape.basis: Graham Rice for the RHS: four-petalled, trumpet-shaped flowers that become more flared as they mature. RHS record: "tulip-shaped". Richard Hawke: the tepals "flare outward like a trumpet as they mature".

flower.tepalTip.basis: Clematis on the Web: "recurved towards tip". International Clematis Society: four sepals with pointed tips that recurve gently.

flower.tepalWidthToLength.basis: Not published. Judged from photographs of flared flowers: a tepal about 5.5 cm long is a little over 2 cm across at its widest.

flower.tubeShareOfLength.basis: Not published. Judged from photographs taken from the side: the tepals stand together as a tube for a little under half their length before they part and turn back.

flower.colourInside.basis: The International Clematis Register, as the International Clematis Society quotes it: "luminous deep slightly mauvish pink with deep pink bar, outside with white margin".

flower.barColour.basis: The International Clematis Register, as the International Clematis Society quotes it: "with deep pink bar". Graham Rice for the RHS: a slightly reddish bar through each petal.

flower.colourOutside.value: pinkish red along the ribs, with a pale margin
flower.colourOutside.basis: The International Clematis Register, as the International Clematis Society quotes it: "outside with white margin". The Society's recommended list: "pinkish red on the outside of the sepals and intense pink on the inside". RHS record: "brighter pink at the margins".

flower.stamenColours.basis: RHS plant record: "with cream and maroon stamens". Clematis on the Web: "Cream-yellow or bright yellow stamens"; the International Clematis Society: creamy stamens with pale yellow anthers.

flower.stamenCount.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Gibson, of the parent C. texensis: "stamens 30-40 in 3 series".

flower.stamenLengthM.basis: Not published. In the parent C. texensis a filament of about 8 mm carries an anther of about 7 mm (Gibson), 15 mm in all; in photographs of the cultivar the boss of stamens is about a third as long as a tepal.

flower.stalkLengthM.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Bean, of the parent C. texensis: flowers "on a ribbed stalk 5 to 6 in. long"; Gibson: peduncle to 170 mm. Photographs of the cultivar show stalks of that order, two flower-lengths or more.

flower.bractCount.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Gibson, of the parent C. texensis: "bracts subtending peduncle 2 and opposite, leaflike". A pair of small leaves on the flower stalk shows in photographs of the cultivar.

flower.bractLengthM.basis: Not published. Gibson gives a blade "to 60 x 40 mm" for the bracts of the parent species; those in photographs of the cultivar are smaller, about half the length of a leaflet.

flower.budShape.value: egg-shaped and pointed, ribbed, downy; green, then pink with paler faces
flower.budShape.basis: Not described in any source read. From photographs of the cultivar (Wikimedia Commons).

fruit.type.value: head of achenes, each with a long feathered tail
fruit.type.basis: International Clematis Society: the seed heads are "gorgeous and persistent"; growers call them silky and ball-shaped. That they are heads of tailed achenes is the genus's fruit: Gibson, of the parent C. texensis, "achenes, to 30 in headlike cluster ... each achene with a long, feathery beak".

fruit.sizeMeasure.value: width of the whole seed head across its tails
fruit.sizeMeasure.basis: What fruit.lengthM in the growth model measures for this taxon, and so what RenderFruit.lengthM carries and the seed-head model is authored to: one unit of the model is this width.

fruit.lengthM.basis: Width of the whole seed head across its feathered tails. Not published for the cultivar. In the parent C. texensis an achene 7.5-10 mm long carries a tail of 27-34 mm (Gibson) or "about 1 1/2 in." (Bean), which makes a head 5 to 7 cm across.

fruit.acheneCount.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Gibson, of the parent C. texensis: "pistils ca. 30" and "achenes, to 30 in headlike cluster".

fruit.acheneLengthM.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Gibson, of the parent C. texensis: achene "7.5-10 x 5-6 x 2 mm".

fruit.tailLengthM.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Of the parent C. texensis: beak "27-34 mm long", "curved to twisted (never straight)" (Gibson); a feathery style "about 1 1/2 in. long" (Bean).

fruit.tailHairLengthM.basis: Not published for the cultivar. Gibson, of the parent C. texensis: the beak "densely pilose with ascending to spreading, golden, straight hairs 2-3+ mm long".

fruit.colourRipe.value: silvery, the tails with golden hairs, the achenes brown
fruit.colourRipe.basis: Not published for the cultivar beyond "silky". Gibson, of the parent C. texensis: achenes "light brown to brown", beak "densely pilose with ... golden, straight hairs".

fruit.persistence.basis: International Clematis Society: the seed heads are "gorgeous and persistent".
